To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of meta-features to estimate the competence level of the classifiers in the pool of classifiers, together with a dynamic weighting approach, improves the performance of a dynamic ensemble selection framework.
the proposed improvements to the framework META-DES, in the training and generalisation phases, are very useful for improving the accuracy of the system.

(i) in the training phase, the use of the meta-features proposed by the authors in the original META-DES paper, combined with the use of the Random Forests algorithm for the training of a meta-classifier, is the best approach; (ii) in the generalization phase of META-DES, the dynamic weighting approach outperforms the other approaches in terms of classification accuracy; and (iii) the use of the hybrid approach is the best option for the META-DES system
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new ensemble selection approaches that are able to dynamically estimate the competence of the base classifiers in a pool and select only the most competent ones to solve a classification problem.
a new framework for dynamic ensemble selection that is based on meta-learning and that can be easily applied to any base learning algorithm.
the design and evaluation of a new dynamic ensemble selection framework, called META- DES, which combines meta-learning with a dynamic weighting approach.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the META-DES-H framework is the best performing approach in this paper.
the META-DES-Hybrid approach is the best approach in the META-DES.

the dynamic weighting approach is the best approach for the generalization phase of META-DES, while for the training phase, the best approach is the one that uses an ensemble of classifiers to train the meta-classifier.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose improvements in the training and generalisation phase of META-DES.
the proposed changes in the training phase of META-DES improve the performance of META-DES in most of the datasets.

the proposed dynamic weighting approach is a promising alternative for the dynamic selection approach, especially for datasets in which the pool is composed of a large number of classifiers, since it can take the competence of all classifiers into account.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamic weighting approach is more accurate than the dynamic selection approach.
the use of a dynamic weighting scheme is a promising approach to improve the recognition accuracy in dynamic ensemble selection techniques.
the use of meta-learning in the training phase and the use of a hybrid approach in the generalization phase can significantly improve the performance of the META- DES framework.
